title: A six-gate falsification framework for diagnosing locus-driven confounding in Mendelian randomization: analysis code, simulation benchmark and frozen results (v1.2.1)
description:
Analysis code and frozen results for a six-gate falsification framework that grades causal claims from Mendelian randomization (association screening, robustness, genetic architecture, direct effect, biological mediation, external validation; 0-12 points, Grade A-D). The insomnia-Alzheimer's disease pair is used as a worked example; the framework itself is calibrated on twelve trait pairs and a 43,200-replicate simulation grid.

What this release contains. Twenty-five R modules and the Python pipeline under code/; a deterministic simulation benchmark (code/sim_framework_operating_chars.py, seed 20260804, 43,200 replicates, about 25 s on one core); the frozen benchmark outputs under results/simulation/, including the post-cap values used in Table 2 and the pre-cap copies kept for the before/after comparison in Supplementary Table S12.5; Supplementary Tables S1-S12 under manuscript/supplementary/; figures under manuscript/figures/; environment specifications for both runtimes (renv.lock for R 4.5.2, code/requirements.txt for Python 3.13.14); and MANIFEST_sha256.csv, which hashes every deposited file so that a reader can confirm their copy and their re-run match the archived one byte for byte.

Changes since v1.0.0. This release supersedes v1.0.0 and v1.1.0. The simulation now applies the framework's decisive-failure rule (failure at the robustness gate caps the total at 6, the upper bound of Grade C), which the earlier deposited script did not implement. Of 43,200 replicates, 4,363 move from Grade B to Grade C, all of them with a true non-zero effect: marginal sensitivity at the largest effect size falls from 0.973 to 0.878 without pleiotropy, from 0.847 to 0.724 under balanced pleiotropy and from 0.804 to 0.691 under directional pleiotropy, while specificity and the Grade A frequency are unchanged. The Table 2 values in this release therefore differ from those in v1.0.0, and the deposited script now reproduces them exactly. The pre-cap outputs are retained under results/simulation/_precap/ for comparison. Supplementary Tables S10-S12 (gate ablation, instrument tiers, threshold and cap robustness) are new.

What is not deposited. Raw and harmonised GWAS summary statistics are not included, both because of size and because they are distributed under their own data-use terms. They are rebuilt from the named source studies by the scripts in code/; the workflow section of the README lists the accessions. The empirical gate scores can therefore be audited against the cited sources but not recomputed from this deposit alone. This limitation is stated in the manuscript.
notes: v1.2.1 accompanies the revised manuscript submitted to Frontiers in Genetics (Methods) and corrects the file manifest of v1.2.0: that manifest hashed the author's CRLF checkout rather than the archived bytes, so 125 of 159 files did not verify on any other machine. The archived content itself is unchanged between v1.2.0 and v1.2.1. Supersedes v1.0.0 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21858125) and v1.1.0, which were deposited under an earlier repository link. Cite the version DOI of this release rather than a concept DOI when referring to specific numerical results, because the benchmark values changed between v1.0.0 and v1.2.0.
